DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Squamous Cell Carcinoma to the Cervical Lymph Nodes (Nuchal Nodes) from a primary Head and Neck Malignancy.

The history of painless, progressively enlarging nuchal lymphadenopathy in a 50-year-old male with a significant smoking history (implied by the occupation and hobbies, though not explicitly stated, the clinical picture is classic) is highly suspicious for metastatic head and neck cancer. Given the location at the nape of the neck and the duration, this likely represents nodal spread from a primary tumor in the oral cavity, oropharynx, or skin of the scalp, rather than the colon cancer which would typically present with hepatic or distant visceral metastases first.
